span.span: I evaluated everything based on whether the requirement was satisfied verbatim, using my own professional judgement when there was ambiguity. If there was a data folder and a look at the trajectory indicated it was real, I allowed it to be loaded directly. If there were results and no clear source code making them, I considered the task incomplete. I didn’t consider a dummy data path to be correct (GPT-Pilot used a lot of these). To determine if something was executed correctly, I skimmed the end of the logs (e.g., trajectory) for any obvious signs of an error. If there wasn’t any, I said it was correctly executed. I ignored prerequisites while evaluating and did not execute anything, instead just eyeballing the code for correctness. I was lenient in what I considered to be sufficient in terms of the more vague requirements (e.g., if the preprocessing had to include scaling and rotation, just those two would be sufficient to consider it done).
